pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: crates/core/migrations/0015_tier_memory.sql:1 A case-insensitive search of crates/core for episod, belief, consolidat, distill and recall found nothing; every 'memory' table in the migrations is the fetcher's per-host strike/penalty router (0015/0016/0033), DataHub governance state (0038) or the event log (0055), so no schema here stores an agent's episodes, beliefs or recall items.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:913 The MCP server tells agents that research/findings and research/sources, read with query_dataset, are 'the agent's memory', but query_dataset returns only the number of rows it picked, with no eligible total and no echoed limit, so an agent cannot tell a complete recall from a truncated one.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:913 The recall result gives only the selected count. The technique requires selected, eligible/considered and budget, so 100 bare rows read as everything the store holds.
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:895 A silent default cap of 100 rows on the memory read path is a loss site, and the result carries no notice that rows were cut.
crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:927 The search tool passes the renderer's index degraded-state block through to the agent, so a wiped or failed lane does not read as an empty success.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject's precondition does not cover a host that keeps no memory pipeline itself but publishes a generic dataset read tool as an external agent's memory. It would help to say which techniques (recall-injection result shape, loss-site notices) still bind such a read surface.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:130 The doc-sync hook reads session transcripts only to collect a turn's file edits, and it explicitly treats the agent memory dir as out of scope; a search of scripts/docs for episod, belief, consolidat, distill and recall found nothing, so no memory store is written or recalled here.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/induce.rs:2 Rule induction is a stateless statistical pass over a page set that the caller supplies, and json_salvage only repairs output; a search of crates/core for episod, belief, consolidat, distill and recall found nothing, so this context keeps no carried-forward agent memory.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/tiers.rs:1 The only 'memory' in this context is the fetcher's per-host tier-routing record (strikes, preferred tier, TTL). It is a learned routing cache, not an LLM agent's working, episodic or consolidated memory, and a search of crates/core for episod, belief, consolidat, distill and recall found nothing.
